name: Porcius Festus
bio: Porcius Festus succeeded Felix as governor after two years, inheriting Paul still held in custody, since Felix had left him bound to please the Jews (Acts 24:27). His further dealings with Paul are told in the chapters ahead. When he became governor, Jewish leaders in Jerusalem pressed Festus to have Paul brought there, but he instead held a hearing in Caesarea; when he suggested trying Paul in Jerusalem, Paul appealed to Caesar, which Festus granted. Unsure how to write up the charges, Festus consulted visiting King Agrippa and Bernice, explaining that the accusation concerned a dead man Paul claimed was alive, and arranged for Agrippa to hear Paul's case directly (Acts 25:1-27). When Paul spoke of the resurrection, Festus interrupted, saying his learning had driven him mad, but afterward agreed privately with Agrippa and Bernice that Paul had done nothing deserving death (Acts 26:24-32).
